title: Esc interrupts — don't spectate a mistake
body: Wrong path? Esc now, then redirect with a specific correction. Letting it finish costs time and poisons context with the wrong approach.
triggers: Claude took a wrong approach and the user waited it out

title: Esc twice = rewind menu
body: Claude Code auto-checkpoints file changes. Double-Esc on empty input (or /rewind) restores code, conversation, or both. Undo for the session, no git needed.
triggers: last few steps went wrong
user asks to undo edits

title: Shift+Tab cycles permission modes
body: Cycles the permission modes — normal, auto-accept, plan. Match the leash to the task instead of approving every edit by hand.
triggers: user approves many edits one by one

title: @ points at a file instead of describing it
body: Type @ and a path (tab-completes) to put the real file in front of Claude. Describing a file you could reference is wasted breath.
triggers: user describes a file in prose

title: ! runs a shell command yourself
body: Start a message with ! to run a command directly, no round-trip through Claude. Best for interactive things like logins that Claude can't drive.
triggers: user needs an interactive command or a quick check

title: /clear between unrelated tasks
body: The most underused habit there is. New task = clean desk. Carrying the last task's corpse into the next one measurably degrades answers.
triggers: a new unrelated topic starts in a long session

title: /context when quality dips
body: Diagnose before you flail. It shows what is actually eating the window — usually one stale file or a dead-end debugging thread.
triggers: answers get sloppier or repetitive deep in a session

title: /btw asks a side question without derailing
body: Answers a side question without adding it to the conversation history, so a mid-task detour costs you no context.
triggers: a tangent question comes up mid-task

title: /add-dir widens the desk deliberately
body: Need a second repo or a sibling folder? Add it explicitly rather than pasting paths and hoping. Deliberate beats accidental scope.
triggers: work spans two directories

title: Old sessions aren't gone — /resume
body: The eternal-session habit is fear of loss. /resume removes the loss, so a bloated session has no excuse. Nostalgia makes Claude dumber.
triggers: user avoids /clear because they might need the history

title: /compact keeps the thread, /clear drops it
body: Mid-task and running long? /compact compresses and continues. Task finished? /clear — compaction still carries the old task's shape forward.
triggers: context is filling up but the task isn't done

title: Plan first, then read the plan like a reviewer
body: The plan is the cheapest place to catch a mistake. Fixing a plan is a sentence; fixing finished work is a rewrite.
triggers: a multi-file or non-trivial task starts

title: Turn every correction into a CLAUDE.md line
body: Do not just fix it — write the rule down so it never recurs. Over weeks this compounds into a sharp description of how you work.
triggers: user corrects the same class of mistake twice

title: Global facts go in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
body: "I'm on Windows/PowerShell", "be concise", "say verified vs assumed" belong once at user level, not copy-pasted into every repo's CLAUDE.md.
triggers: user re-explains their environment in a new project

title: /init writes the first CLAUDE.md for you
body: Let it draft the project facts, then add your own rules on top. Starting from blank is the reason most projects never get one.
triggers: a project has no CLAUDE.md

title: Three settings scopes, three audiences
body: ~/.claude/settings.json = you everywhere. .claude/settings.json = this project, everyone (commit it). .claude/settings.local.json = just you.
triggers: a permission or env var needs to be saved

title: Fact → CLAUDE.md, procedure → skill, law → hook
body: A procedure stuffed into CLAUDE.md costs tokens every session; an "always do X" prompt gets forgotten — that is a hook's job.
triggers: user is deciding where to put a rule

title: "There's probably a skill for this"
body: Don't memorize the catalog. When a task feels specialized, structured, or repetitive, pause and ask. Type / to see what's actually installed.
triggers: a task feels specialized or repetitive

title: Check /plugin before building from scratch
body: Before writing a skill or hook yourself, look whether a ready one exists. Marketplaces already cover most common workflows.
triggers: user is about to build a skill or hook

title: Slash commands and skills are the same thing now
body: `.claude/commands/deploy.md` and `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` both make /deploy. The real axis is who invokes it — `disable-model-invocation: true` for manual-only.
triggers: user asks whether to make a command or a skill

title: Bottle any prompt you retype
body: "Write a commit message for this", "review my changes" — a prompt you rewrite constantly is a tax you pay every time. A slash command pays it once.
triggers: user types a near-identical prompt a third time

title: "Use subagents" to keep your context clean
body: Big exploratory jobs flood your window with noise. A subagent works in its own context and hands back only the conclusion.
triggers: a broad search across many files is starting

title: Run parallel sessions for independent tasks
body: Two unrelated jobs don't belong in one session fighting for the same context window. Open a second terminal.
triggers: two unrelated tasks are queued

title: "Always do X" is a hook, not a prompt
body: "Run the linter after every edit" shouldn't be a request Claude occasionally forgets — it should be a law the harness enforces. That's what hooks are.
triggers: user repeats a standing instruction

title: Automate only after the shape stops moving
body: A hook, loop, or routine earns its keep once a task is stable and repeated. Automating something still changing just creates a rigid thing to fight.
triggers: user wants to automate a first-time workflow

title: Routines run while you're not there
body: "Every weekday 8am, summarize what changed" is a scheduled agent, not something you should be awake for. Perfect for briefings and watchers.
triggers: user does the same check every morning

title: /loop repeats a task on an interval
body: For polling something that changes on its own — a CI run, a deploy, a queue. Omit the interval and Claude paces itself.
triggers: user is manually re-checking an external process

title: Model choice is per-task, not per-life
body: Haiku = fast/simple, Sonnet = daily driver, Opus = hard/high-stakes, Fable = enormous. Switch freely mid-session as the work changes.
triggers: a session shifts between trivial and hard work

title: Climb when it visibly struggles
body: Going in circles, missing cross-file implications, or confidently wrong twice? That's the signal to move up a model — not to re-prompt louder.
triggers: the same problem fails twice

title: Effort is a second, separate dial
body: Model = how big a brain. Effort = how long it thinks. low for trivial, xhigh for hard agentic coding, max for must-not-fail. Max on everything is just slower.
triggers: an answer feels shallow on a hard problem

title: /fast speeds up Opus without downgrading it
body: Same brain, quicker delivery. When you want speed but the task still deserves Opus, that's the lever — not dropping down the ladder.
triggers: user wants speed on a task that needs Opus

title: Fluent is not correct
body: Risk spikes on specific checkable claims: API signatures, flags, versions, citations. Uniform confidence across easy and hard claims is itself a tell.
triggers: Claude states an exact API, flag, or citation

title: Ask for the source before the answer
body: "Quote the exact lines you are basing this on." Grounds the answer in real text. If it cannot produce the quote, that is your answer.
triggers: a factual claim matters and is checkable

title: The re-ask test
body: Ask the same question in a fresh session with no prior context. Consistency isn't proof of truth, but inconsistency is proof of a problem.
triggers: a suspicious answer needs a second opinion

title: Give permission to not know
body: "If you're not sure, say so — I'd rather have 'I don't know' than a confident guess." One sentence in CLAUDE.md measurably reduces fabrication.
triggers: a confident answer turns out to be invented

title: In code you have a truth machine
body: The compiler, the type checker, and the tests don't hallucinate. Don't read generated code and nod — run it. Verification is a keystroke away.
triggers: code is written but not executed

title: Read the diff, don't trust "done"
body: The visual diff is right there. "It said it fixed it" is not verification — the whole point of the loop is that reality referees.
triggers: a change is reported complete

title: The loop: explore → plan → code → verify → commit → review
body: Then /clear and start the next task with a clean desk. Without the loop, AI coding degenerates into generate-and-pray.
triggers: a feature is being built end to end

title: Commit often so every change is a cheap revert
body: Small frequent commits turn "it mangled everything" into "git reset and try again." Work fearlessly because you can undo.
triggers: a risky or large change is about to start

title: Risky experiment → a worktree
body: About to let it loose on something you might want to throw away? Branch into a worktree first — your main tree stays untouched either way.
triggers: an experimental refactor is starting

title: Two corrections haven't landed? Stop arguing
body: A third "no, like I said…" into a context full of the misunderstanding rarely works. Rewind or /clear and re-ask fresh.
triggers: the same correction is given a third time

title: Match the undo to the size of the mistake
body: Shallow → raise effort. Degrading → /context then /clear. Last steps wrong → /rewind. Whole approach wrong → git reset. Nuking a session over one bad step wastes good context.
triggers: something went wrong and the fix size is unclear

title: /usage shows what you're actually burning
body: Big model + max effort + subagent swarms is a fine choice when chosen. Glance at the gauge after a heavy session so it stays a choice.
triggers: after a heavy session or a big fan-out

title: Say what was wrong, don't repeat louder
body: Volume as strategy is the tourist move. "Drier tone, cut the last paragraph" beats re-typing the whole request. Converging beats gambling.
triggers: user re-sends a similar prompt after a miss

title: One example beats a paragraph of description
body: When the format matters, paste a sample of the output you want. Describing a shape is strictly worse than showing it.
triggers: output format keeps coming out wrong

title: Give the "because"
body: The constraint behind the request is what lets Claude decide everything you did not specify. "Make it fast" and "fast because it runs per-keystroke" are different jobs.
triggers: a request has an unstated constraint

title: Use Claude to get better at Claude
body: "Rewrite my prompt to get a better result and tell me what you changed." Or "skill, command, or hook?" The tool teaches itself if you ask.
triggers: user is unsure how to phrase or where to put something

title: Feed it eyes — paste the screenshot
body: An error, a UI, a diagram. Describing an image in words when you could paste it is wasted effort and a lossy channel.
triggers: user describes a visual bug or a UI in prose

title: Right surface, right job
body: Codebase → Code. Documents, no terminal → Cowork. Think/write → Chat. Recurring while you sleep → Routine. Forcing every job into your comfort-room is a quiet tax.
triggers: a non-code task is being done in the terminal

title: MCP tool permissions are mcp__server__tool
body: `mcp__` prefix, then the name you gave the server at `claude mcp add`, then the tool. /mcp shows which servers are connected and where OAuth is stuck.
triggers: an MCP tool needs allowlisting or a server looks down

title: The one-liner reflex
body: Firing a vague prompt and taking whatever bounces back. The fix is not a longer prompt — it is naming the goal, the constraint, and what done looks like.
triggers: a vague request gets a generic answer

title: The eternal session is 80% noise
body: Symptom check: if you cannot say in one sentence what this session is about, it is already too full to answer well.
triggers: a session has covered three unrelated topics

title: claude -p runs headless, for scripts and CI
body: Same agent loop, no TUI. Pipe input in, get output out — that's how Claude Code becomes a step in a pipeline instead of a thing you sit in front of.
triggers: a task should run unattended or in CI

title: A subagent cannot see your session
body: It starts blind. Give it the paths, the naming conventions, and what a good answer looks like — a vague delegation comes back vague.
triggers: work is about to be delegated to a subagent

title: Make it read before it plans
body: "Read the relevant files and tell me what you found, then stop." A plan built on assumptions is a confident plan for the wrong codebase.
triggers: a plan is being written for unfamiliar code
